title: 7 Day Gifts Before the Wedding: Ideas for Each Day
metaTitle: 7 Day Gifts Before the Wedding: Ideas for Each Day
description: A simple day-by-day plan for the seven gifts before a Jewish wedding: sentimental, practical, fun and one bigger gift, with ideas for the chosson and the kallah.
intro: Some couples send each other a small gift every day of the week before the wedding. It is a sweet way to stay connected and build excitement, but planning seven gifts on top of everything else can feel like a lot.
If you want a starting point, here is one easy way to plan the week: a different theme for each day, so the gifts feel varied without overthinking it.

sections.heading: Day 1: Something sentimental
sections.text: Start the week with something that is really about the two of you. A box of letters to open at different moments, or a card with your own photos, sets the tone for the whole week.

sections.heading: Day 2: Something cozy to wear
sections.text: Comfortable, wearable gifts get used right away, and they are easy to send.

sections.heading: Day 3: Something for every day
sections.text: Pick something they will carry or use daily, so they think of you every time they reach for it. Personalizing it with initials makes it feel special.

sections.heading: Day 4: Something for your new home
sections.text: A gift for the home you are about to start together: a blanket with your wedding date, a book for your family recipes, or a photo calendar.

sections.heading: Day 5: Something for the trip ahead
sections.text: Sheva brachos often means a week of going from place to place, and many couples travel afterward. Practical travel gifts help.

sections.heading: Day 6: Something fun
sections.text: By now emotions run high, and a laugh helps. A funny gift, or something to do together after the wedding, keeps it light.

sections.heading: Day 7: The special one
sections.text: Many people save a bigger or more meaningful gift for the last day, or for the wedding day itself.

tips: Order personalized and engraved items first. Personalized gifts take longer to make and ship, so check each listing's delivery estimate before you count on it.
Plan who will deliver each gift. A sibling, friend or parent often brings it over, so have everything wrapped and labeled by day.
A short handwritten note with each gift often means more than the gift itself.
Mix price points. A few small gifts and one bigger one usually feels more balanced than seven expensive ones.

title: Gifts for the Kallah: Thoughtful Ideas for the Week Before the Wedding
metaTitle: Gifts for the Kallah: Ideas for the Week Before the Wedding
description: Gift ideas for a kallah from her chosson: keepsakes, fragrance, cozy gifts and travel pieces for sheva brachos and beyond.
intro: Looking for something for your kallah? The best gifts for the week before the wedding tend to be personal rather than expensive: something that shows you thought about her, that she can use in your new home, or that she will keep for years.
Here are ideas grouped by the kind of gift. Mix a few small ones with one bigger gift if you are planning all seven days.

sections.heading: Keepsakes she will hold on to
sections.text: Personalized pieces with her name, your initials or your wedding date.

sections.heading: Fragrance and getting ready
sections.text: A special fragrance or a pretty organizer for her things.

sections.heading: For sheva brachos and travel
sections.text: Practical pieces for a busy week of simchas and any trip afterward.

sections.heading: Cozy and everyday
sections.text: Gifts she will use at home every day.

tips: If you are not sure about her taste in fragrance or style, ask her sister or a close friend.
Personalized items need extra time to arrive, so order them first.

title: Gifts for the Chosson: Ideas He Will Actually Use
metaTitle: Gifts for the Chosson: Ideas He Will Actually Use
description: Gift ideas for a chosson from his kallah: personalized everyday carry, gifts for shiur and the desk, travel gear and a few fun picks.
intro: The ideas here focus on personal touches a kallah can send during the week before the wedding: things he will carry every day, use on the go, or that simply make him smile.
Personalizing a simple item with his initials is an easy way to make it feel like it came from you.

sections.heading: Everyday carry
sections.text: Small, useful things he will have with him every day.

sections.heading: For shiur, work and the desk
sections.text: Classic gifts for writing and keeping organized.

sections.heading: For the trip ahead
sections.text: Travel gear for sheva brachos week and beyond.

sections.heading: A little fun
sections.text: Hobbies, hosting and a few things just for him.

tips: Think about what he already uses every day (a wallet, a phone, a pen) and upgrade it.
Engraving and monograms take extra time, so order those first.

title: Personalized Gifts: Thoughtful Ideas With Your Photo or Names
metaTitle: Personalized Gifts With Your Photo or Names: Thoughtful Ideas
description: Personalized gift ideas with your photo, names, initials or wedding date: blankets, photo keepsakes, jewelry boxes, engraved gifts for him and more.
intro: A gift with your photo, your names or your wedding date on it says something a store-bought gift can't: that you sat down and thought about this person. It is usually the gift that gets kept, used and shown off long after the wrapping is gone.
Here are personalized ideas grouped by what goes on them, plus picks just for her and just for him. Most take a few extra days to make, so order these first.

sections.heading: With your photo
sections.text: Turn a favorite picture of the two of you into something to hold, hang up or snuggle under.

sections.heading: With your names or wedding date
sections.text: Keepsakes for both of you and your new home, with your names, initials or the date.

sections.heading: Personalized for her
sections.text: Pretty, useful pieces with her name or initials on them.

sections.heading: Personalized for him
sections.text: Engraved and monogrammed things he will carry and use every day.

tips: Double-check spelling and dates before you order. A typo is the one thing you can't fix later.
Personalized items usually take a few extra days to make and ship, so order them before anything else.
Pick a clear, well-lit photo for photo gifts; faces close to the camera print best.

title: Gifts for Her: Ideas She Will Love and Actually Use
metaTitle: Gifts for Her: Thoughtful Ideas She Will Love and Use
description: Gift ideas for her: fragrance, jewelry storage, cozy slippers and throws, gadgets she will use every day and fun for her free time.
intro: The best gifts for her are the ones she would love but wouldn't buy for herself: a fragrance she has been eyeing, something soft for slow mornings at home, or a gadget that makes her day a little easier.
Here are ideas grouped by the kind of gift, at a range of budgets. Looking for something with her name or your photo on it? See our personalized gifts guide.

sections.heading: Fragrance and pretty things
sections.text: A special scent and lovely places to keep her jewelry.

sections.heading: Cozy at home
sections.text: Soft slippers and throws for Shabbos mornings and quiet evenings.

sections.heading: Gadgets she will use every day
sections.text: Useful tech that makes reading, listening and her morning coffee better.

sections.heading: For her free time
sections.text: Something fun to do with friends, on the court or on a getaway.

tips: Not sure about fragrance? Ask her sister or a close friend what she wears, or pick a gadget or cozy gift instead.
Check her size before ordering slippers. Most of these run true to size, but returns are a hassle.
One bigger gift with a short handwritten note usually means more than several small ones.

title: Gifts for Him: Ideas He Will Use Every Day
metaTitle: Gifts for Him: Thoughtful Ideas He Will Use Every Day
description: Gift ideas for him: cologne, sterling silver collar stays, wallets and everyday carry, desk upgrades, cozy slippers and fun gadgets.
intro: Men are famously hard to shop for, but the gifts that land usually have one thing in common: he will use them every day. A great cologne, a sharp everyday-carry upgrade or something for his desk beats another gadget that ends up in a drawer.
Here are ideas grouped by the kind of gift, at a range of budgets. Want his name or initials on it? See our personalized gifts guide.

sections.heading: Cologne
sections.text: A signature scent he will wear to work, shul and simchas.

sections.heading: Everyday carry
sections.text: Small upgrades he will have on him every single day.

sections.heading: For his desk and nightstand
sections.text: A neater desk, a charged phone and a home for his watch and keys.

sections.heading: Cozy at home
sections.text: Slippers and loafers for Shabbos mornings and relaxing evenings.

sections.heading: Hobbies and fun
sections.text: Something new to try or a better version of what he already loves.

tips: Collar stays are an easy win: 2.25 inch stays fit most dress shirts, including Charles Tyrwhitt.
Not sure which cologne? Fresh, citrusy scents like Light Blue Pour Homme or Luna Rossa Ocean are a safe first pick.
Pair a small everyday item with a short note so he thinks of you each time he uses it.

title: Chanukah Gifts for Your Wife or Husband
metaTitle: Chanukah Gifts for Your Wife or Husband
description: Chanukah gift ideas for your spouse: cozy gifts, keepsakes and useful tech for her, for him and for the two of you.
intro: Some couples give one gift for Chanukah, others give something small on each of the eight nights. Either way, it is a nice chance to give your husband or wife something that fits your life together right now.
Here are ideas for her, for him, and for the two of you to enjoy together.

sections.heading: For your wife
sections.text: Gifts that are cozy, beautiful or simply make her day easier.

sections.heading: For your husband
sections.text: Useful, comfortable and a little bit special.

sections.heading: For both of you
sections.text: Gifts to enjoy together on a Chanukah night at home.

tips: Planning eight nights? Mix a few small, fun gifts with one bigger gift for a special night.
Order early in the season, since popular items and personalized gifts can take longer to arrive in December.
